attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the Harbour Harriers Open Race Half Marathon, Sunday 28 November 2027

From Owen Cartwright, Club Chair, Harbour Harriers Athletic Club

The race is a half marathon with 220 runners and starts at 08:30. We are talking to Halden Medical Transport about ambulance cover; see the attached.

First aid
Several of our members have done the first aid course through work, and they're happy to help out. We keep a good first aid box at the HQ tent, and another one goes in the lead car. In all our years we've only ever had blisters and scraped knees.

Heat, cold and water
There's water every 2.5 km. We look at the forecast two days before and again two hours before. Over 28 degrees we start earlier or cut the course, and over 32 degrees we call it off. If it's cold or wet, we have foil blankets and a warm tent at the finish.

If someone needs hospital
If someone needed the hospital we'd dial 911 and the paramedics would take it from there. They know what they're doing far better than we do, and the city's service is very good.

Staying in touch
We'll all have our phones, and I'll send a list of numbers round the team the week before. The signal is usually fine around there.

In recent years the last runner has usually finished well inside the time limit, and past incidents have been limited to a few blisters and one twisted ankle. A number of members have first aid certificates from work and are glad to be there in a general helping role.

Who's responsible
Our medical lead is Carl Jensen, a registered paramedic, who'll be there from an hour before the start until the last runner is in and has the final word on pulling any runner out.
